statement: For the planar Kepler problem with GM=a=1 over 20 periods, fixed-step kick-drift-kick leapfrog has maximum sampled position error below 0.01a for the following finite cases only: (e,N)=(0,2048),(0.3,2048),(0.6,4096),(0.6,8192), where N is steps per 2π period. This is a resolution-qualified finite-case replacement; it makes no claim for intervening N, other eccentricities, or arbitrary higher-resolution monotonicity.
acceptance: Each named case must complete 20 periods with maximum sampled Euclidean position error versus the same-time analytic Kepler solution <0.01a. Kepler-equation residual, initial-state mismatch, and period consistency must each be <=1e-11; an independently converged DOP853 integration must agree with the exact-reference maximum position error to <=1e-7a. Also report maximum relative energy error. The separate e=0.6,N=2048 probe is an out-of-domain falsifier probe, not part of the repair acceptance set.
rationale: The original implication failed because bounded energy error did not control accumulated phase error. Rather than fit a universal threshold from the original grid, this repair states four prospective, conservative finite resolution cases. N=2048 is well above the known circular N=512 pass and the e=0.3 N=512 failure; N=4096 is chosen for e=0.6 based on its more severe periapsis dynamics. A lower-resolution e=0.6,N=2048 probe is included to seek a further counterexample to any broader reading.
